title: Unveiling and Mitigating Bias in Mental Health Analysis with Large Language Models
findings: Models generally struggled more with the religion demographic factor compared to gender and age, showing greater variability in performance and fairness. This indicates more pronounced bias related to religion. For example, models were found to predict mental health issues more frequently for users mentioning Islam, suggesting a bias that unfairly associates religious practices with mental health concerns.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured predictive bias in mental health classification tasks. Specifically, it evaluated whether Large Language Models exhibited different performance (F1 score) and fairness (Equalized Odds) when the user's religious identity was provided as context for a given text.
